concepts.def: Demographic Transition Model; 5 stages from high BR+DR to low BR+DR.
Births per 1000 per year (crude birth rate).
Deaths per 1000 per year (crude death rate).

walkthroughs.body_html: Stage 1: high stationary (BR 35-50, DR 30-40); pre-industrial. Stage 2: early expanding; DR falls first as medicine improves. Stage 3: late expanding; BR falls as urbanisation/education spread. Stage 4: low stationary (BR 10-15, DR 9-12). Stage 5: declining (BR < DR).

UK Stage 1 to 1750; Stage 2 1750-1880 with Industrial Revolution; Stage 3 1880-1940 with sanitation and education; Stage 4 by 1950. Currently Stage 4-5: BR 10.5/1000, DR 9.5/1000 (2022). TFR 1.49 below replacement. Net migration sustains population.

Niger BR 47/1000 (highest globally), DR 8/1000 in 2022. TFR 6.7 children per woman. Median age 14.8 years; 50 percent of population under 15. Drivers: low female education, religious values, agricultural economy, polygyny. Population to triple by 2050.

mcqs.q: Why is the Demographic Transition Model criticised for not applying to all countries?
options: The DTM only applies to countries with more than 50 million people.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
All countries follow the five stages of the DTM in order.

It was based on European industrialisation. LICs today face different conditions: imported medicine without industrialisation, cultural factors, gender inequality and globalised economies — not all follow the same path.

mcqs.q: What happens in Stage 2 of the Demographic Transition Model?
options: Birth rates rise rapidly because people want larger families.
Death rates fall rapidly (due to better food, sanitation and medicine) while birth rates remain high, causing rapid population growth.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
Rostow's model is universally accepted as the best development theory.

mcqs.q: What is the main criticism of Rostow's stages of economic growth?
options: It assumes all countries can follow the same linear Western industrialisation path, ignoring colonial legacies, global trade inequalities and environmental constraints — a top-down modernisation view.
Both birth and death rates fall sharply in Stage 2.
All LICs will pass through Rostow's five stages if they wait long enough.
Rostow's model is universally accepted as the best development theory.
